name: Walled Historic Village
description: The heart of Monsaraz: whitewashed cobbled lanes, the hilltop castle, and sweeping views over the Alqueva reservoir and Alentejo plains. Pedestrian-only and tiny, with a handful of guesthouses, cafes, and craft shops. Deeply atmospheric but very quiet outside daytime tourist hours, and cars must be parked just outside the walls.
bestFor: short stays, history lovers, photographers, solo remote workers wanting solitude
pros: Extraordinary views and preserved medieval atmosphere
cons: No coworking and unreliable wifi in older buildings
Very limited shops, services, and nightlife

name: Telheiro (Below the Walls)
tagline: The quieter slope beneath the castle
description: A small residential area just outside and below the fortified village, with modest houses, a few local businesses, and easier car access than the walled center. Popular with residents and longer-term renters who want proximity to Monsaraz without the tourist foot traffic of the walls. Still very small and rural, with the same reliance on driving for errands.
bestFor: longer-term renters, people who want a car parked at home, budget-conscious stays
pros: Easier parking and car access than inside the walls
Slightly lower rents than the historic center
Still walking distance to the village and viewpoints
cons: Fewer amenities than the walled village itself
Still no coworking or reliable public transit

name: Alqueva Lakeside (near Monsaraz Marina)
tagline: Waterfront calm on Europe's largest reservoir
description: The shoreline area below the village where the Alqueva reservoir meets small marinas and beach clubs, offering boating, kayaking, and lake swimming in summer. A more resort-like, seasonal feel compared to the village above, with a few lakeside restaurants and rental cottages. Popular for day trips and short stays rather than permanent living.
bestFor: watersports fans, families, short scenic stays, stargazing trips
pros: Direct access to swimming, boating, and lake activities
Beautiful sunset and Dark Sky stargazing spot
Cooler by the water during hot summer days
cons: Sparse amenities and largely seasonal operation
Requires a car to reach the village or any real services

name: Reguengos de Monsaraz
tagline: The nearby market town with real infrastructure
description: A proper small town about 15 minutes' drive from Monsaraz, with supermarkets, pharmacies, banks, schools, and a wider choice of restaurants and wine cellars from the surrounding Alentejo wine region. Many long-stay remote workers base themselves here instead of the village itself for practicality, while still visiting Monsaraz regularly for its scenery and quiet.
bestFor: long-term remote workers, families, anyone wanting groceries and services nearby
pros: Full range of everyday services and shops
More affordable and varied housing options
Still close enough for regular Monsaraz visits
cons: Less dramatic scenery than the hilltop village itself
Still requires a car for regional travel and Evora trips
